```{r setup}
#| include: false
library(reticulate)
library(tidyverse)
library(fixated)
use_python(Sys.getenv("RETICULATE_PYTHON", unset = Sys.which("python3")), required = TRUE)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
```

## Workflow

1. **Python (pymovements)**: read the raw EyeLink ASC file, convert pixels to degrees, compute velocities, detect fixations.
2. **R ([fixated](https://github.com/bernhardangele/fixated), tidyverse, lme4)**: merge fixations with word regions, compute reading measures (FFD, GD, GPT, TVT, ...), run statistics.

All results are computed from a **real binocular EyeLink recording**
(`data/sub_1_example.asc`, Spanish sentence reading, 1000 Hz, 4 trials), the example file shipped with `fixated`.

## Reading the ASC file

```{python}
import numpy as np
import polars as pl
import pymovements as pm

gaze_raw = pm.gaze.from_asc("data/sub_1_example.asc", messages=True)
messages = gaze_raw.messages.with_columns(pl.col("time").cast(pl.Int64))
gaze_raw.samples.head(3)
```

Samples are binocular: `pixel` holds `[x_left, y_left, x_right, y_right]`.

## Trials and word boundaries from the messages

```{python}
trials = (
    messages.filter(pl.col("content").str.contains(r"^start_trial|^DISPLAY (ON|OFF)"))
    .with_columns(
        pl.col("content").str.extract(r"^start_trial (\d+)", 1).cast(pl.Int64).forward_fill().alias("trial")
    )
    .filter(pl.col("content").str.starts_with("DISPLAY"))
    .group_by("trial", maintain_order=True)
    .agg(
        pl.col("time").filter(pl.col("content") == "DISPLAY ON").first().alias("display_on"),
        pl.col("time").filter(pl.col("content") == "DISPLAY OFF").first().alias("display_off"),
    )
)

words = (
    messages.filter(pl.col("content").str.contains(r"^TRIAL \d+ ITEM"))
    .with_columns(
        pl.col("content").str.extract_groups(
            r"^TRIAL (?P<trial>\d+) ITEM (?P<item>\d+) WORD (?P<word_id>\d+) (?P<word>\S+) RIGHT_BOUNDARY (?P<x_end>\d+)"
        ).alias("d")
    )
    .unnest("d")
    .with_columns(pl.col(c).cast(pl.Int64) for c in ["trial", "item", "word_id", "x_end"])
    .drop("time", "content")
    .sort("trial", "word_id")
    # the left edge of a word is the right boundary of the previous one
    .with_columns(pl.col("x_end").shift(1).over("trial").fill_null(0).alias("x_start"))
)
trials
```

## Preprocessing with pymovements

Only left-eye samples between `DISPLAY ON` and `DISPLAY OFF` are used.
The screen geometry (53 x 29.8 cm at 60 cm) gives ~40 px/deg, matching the resolution reported by the EyeLink.

```{python}
samples = (
    gaze_raw.samples
    .with_columns(pl.col("pixel").list.get(0).alias("x_pix"), pl.col("pixel").list.get(1).alias("y_pix"))
    .select("time", "x_pix", "y_pix")
    .join_where(trials, pl.col("time") >= pl.col("display_on"), pl.col("time") <= pl.col("display_off"))
    .select("time", "trial", "x_pix", "y_pix")
)

experiment = pm.Experiment(
    screen_width_px=1920, screen_height_px=1080,
    screen_width_cm=53, screen_height_cm=29.8,
    distance_cm=60, sampling_rate=1000,
)
gaze = pm.Gaze(
    samples=samples, experiment=experiment,
    time_column="time", time_unit="ms",
    pixel_columns=["x_pix", "y_pix"], trial_columns="trial",
)
gaze.pix2deg()
gaze.pos2vel("savitzky_golay", degree=2, window_length=7)
gaze.samples.head(3)
```

## Fixation detection: two algorithms

- **I-DT** (dispersion): a fixation is a window of samples whose spatial spread stays below a threshold (1 deg) for at least 80 ms.
- **Engbert & Kliegl** (velocity, adaptive): saccades are samples whose 2D velocity exceeds an elliptic threshold
  of 6 median-based standard deviations *of that trial's own velocity noise*; fixations are what lies between saccades.

```{python}
def with_location(fix, samples):
    """Mean pixel position of the samples within each fixation."""
    mean_pos = (
        fix.join_where(samples, pl.col("time") >= pl.col("onset"), pl.col("time") <= pl.col("offset"),
                       suffix="_s")
        .filter(pl.col("trial") == pl.col("trial_s"))
        .group_by("trial", "onset", "offset", "duration", maintain_order=True)
        .agg(pl.col("x_pix").mean().alias("avg_x"), pl.col("y_pix").mean().alias("avg_y"))
    )
    return mean_pos.rename({"onset": "start_time", "offset": "end_time"})

# I-DT
gaze.detect("idt", dispersion_threshold=1.0, minimum_duration=80, name="fixation")
fix_idt = with_location(
    gaze.events.frame.filter(pl.col("name") == "fixation").select("trial", "onset", "offset", "duration"),
    samples,
)

# Engbert & Kliegl (2003; Engbert & Mergenthaler 2006 threshold): detect saccades per trial, then fill the gaps
ek = []
for (trial,), sub in gaze.samples.group_by("trial", maintain_order=True):
    sacc = pm.events.microsaccades(sub["velocity"], timesteps=sub["time"], minimum_duration=6, threshold_factor=6)
    fix = pm.events.fill(sacc, timesteps=sub["time"], minimum_duration=40, name="fixation")
    ek.append(fix.frame.with_columns(pl.lit(trial).cast(pl.Int64).alias("trial")))
fix_ek = with_location(pl.concat(ek).select("trial", "onset", "offset", "duration"), samples)

fixations = fix_ek  # used for the reading measures below
fix_ek.head(5)
```

## Comparing the algorithms with EyeLink

```{python}
el = pm.gaze.from_asc("data/sub_1_example.asc", events=True).events.frame
fix_el = (
    el.filter((pl.col("name") == "fixation_eyelink") & (pl.col("eye") == "left"))
    .join_where(trials, pl.col("onset") >= pl.col("display_on"), pl.col("onset") <= pl.col("display_off"))
    .select("trial", "duration")
)
pl.concat([
    fix_idt.select("trial", "duration").with_columns(pl.lit("pymovements I-DT").alias("source")),
    fix_ek.select("trial", "duration").with_columns(pl.lit("pymovements Engbert & Kliegl").alias("source")),
    fix_el.with_columns(pl.lit("EyeLink (left eye)").alias("source")),
]).group_by("source").agg(
    pl.len().alias("n"), pl.col("duration").mean().round(1).alias("mean_ms"), pl.col("duration").median().alias("median_ms")
).sort("source")
```

## Why do they differ?

- The EyeLink parser is also velocity/acceleration based (30 deg/s, 8000 deg/s^2 defaults) with *fixed* thresholds, so it
  behaves like Engbert & Kliegl; the adaptive EK threshold adjusts to noise in each trial.
- I-DT ignores velocity: slow drifts or glissades after a saccade stay inside the dispersion window and are merged
  into the fixation, while small saccades between nearby fixations can be missed. Its minimum duration (80 ms) also removes many short fixations.
- Differences in fixation counts and durations propagate into word-level measures (see below).

## Scanpath of trial 0 (shifted by 25 px for visibility)

```{python}
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

t0 = fixations.filter(pl.col("trial") == 0)
w0 = words.filter(pl.col("trial") == 0)
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 3))
for row in w0.iter_rows(named=True):
    ax.axvspan(row["x_start"], row["x_end"], alpha=0.15 if row["word_id"] % 2 else 0.05, color="k")
    ax.text((row["x_start"] + row["x_end"]) / 2, 1040, row["word"], ha="center", fontsize=8)
ax.plot(t0["avg_x"], t0["avg_y"], "-o", color="C0", label="Engbert & Kliegl")
i0 = fix_idt.filter(pl.col("trial") == 0)
ax.plot(i0["avg_x"], i0["avg_y"] + 25, "--s", color="C1", alpha=0.7, label="I-DT")
ax.legend(loc="lower right")
ax.set_xlim(0, 1100); ax.set_ylim(1080, 500); ax.set_xlabel("x (px)"); ax.set_ylabel("y (px)")
plt.show()
```

## Handing over to R

```{r}
fix <- py$fixations |> as_tibble() |> mutate(eye = "L", trial = as.integer(trial))
roi <- py$words |> as_tibble() |>
  mutate(across(c(trial, item, word_id, x_start, x_end), as.integer), y_start = 0L, y_end = 1080L) |>
  select(trial, item, word_id, word, x_start, x_end, y_start, y_end)
head(fix)
```

## Reading measures with fixated

```{r}
measures <- compute_eye_measures(
  fixations = fix, roi = roi,
  trial_col = "trial", eye_col = "eye",
  shorttime = 80
)
measures |> select(trial, word_id, word, ffd, gd, gpt, tvt, nfix, oreg, ireg) |> head(12)
```

## Do the algorithms change the reading measures?

```{r}
fix_idt <- py$fix_idt |> as_tibble() |> mutate(eye = "L", trial = as.integer(trial))
m_idt <- compute_eye_measures(fix_idt, roi, trial_col = "trial", eye_col = "eye", shorttime = 80)

bind_rows(`Engbert & Kliegl` = measures, `I-DT` = m_idt, .id = "algorithm") |>
  group_by(algorithm) |>
  summarise(across(c(ffd, gd, tvt), \(x) round(mean(x, na.rm = TRUE), 1)), p_fixated = round(mean(pfix), 2))
```

## Word-level summary

```{r}
measures |>
  summarise(
    p_fixated = mean(pfix),
    across(c(ffd, gd, gpt, tvt), \(x) mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)),
    p_regression_out = mean(oreg, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) round(x, 2)))
```

## Statistics: word length and gaze duration

Only four sentences are available, so the model demonstrates the workflow rather than testing a hypothesis.

```{r}
library(lmerTest)
d <- measures |>
  mutate(word_length = str_length(str_remove_all(word, "[[:punct:]]"))) |>
  filter(!is.na(gd), gd > 0) |>
  mutate(word_length_c = word_length - mean(word_length))

m <- lmer(log(gd) ~ word_length_c + (1 | trial), data = d)
round(summary(m)$coefficients, 3)
```

```{r}
ggplot(d, aes(word_length, gd)) +
  geom_point() + geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
  labs(x = "Word length (letters)", y = "Gaze duration (ms)")
```

## Word frequency effect

Frequencies are Zipf values from **SUBTLEX-ESP** (Cuetos et al., 2011; Spanish subtitles), the Spanish counterpart of SUBTLEX-US.
The ASC file lost the accents (`Ser?`, `cr?ticas`); these are resolved to the most frequent accented form that fits.

```{r}
subtlex <- read_tsv(Sys.getenv("SUBTLEX_ESP", "data/SUBTLEX-ESP_form_zipf.txt"),
                    col_names = c("form", "zipf"), col_types = "cd", progress = FALSE)

lookup_zipf <- function(w) {
  w <- str_to_lower(str_remove_all(w, "[[:punct:]]"))
  exact <- subtlex$zipf[match(w, subtlex$form)]
  if (!str_detect(w, fixed("?")) || !is.na(exact)) return(exact)
  # "?" replaced the accented letter: take the most frequent form with a non-ASCII letter at that position
  cand <- subtlex |> filter(str_detect(form, paste0("^", str_replace_all(w, fixed("?"), "[^a-z]"), "$")))
  if (nrow(cand)) max(cand$zipf) else NA_real_
}

freq <- measures |>
  mutate(zipf = map_dbl(word, lookup_zipf), word_length = str_length(str_remove_all(word, "[[:punct:]]")))
cat(sum(!is.na(freq$zipf)), "of", nrow(freq), "words found in SUBTLEX-ESP\n")
freq |> filter(trial == 0) |> select(word, zipf, ffd, gd, tvt) |> head(10)
```

## Frequency effect on gaze duration

```{r}
dz <- freq |>
  filter(!is.na(gd), gd > 0, !is.na(zipf)) |>
  mutate(zipf_c = zipf - mean(zipf), word_length_c = word_length - mean(word_length))

m_freq <- lmer(log(gd) ~ zipf_c + word_length_c + (1 | trial), data = dz)
round(summary(m_freq)$coefficients, 3)
```

```{r}
ggplot(dz, aes(zipf, gd)) +
  geom_point() + geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
  labs(x = "Word frequency (Zipf, SUBTLEX-ESP)", y = "Gaze duration (ms)")
```

A negative `zipf_c` coefficient means that more frequent words are read faster. With four sentences (one participant) this is only a demonstration.

## Time-course (visual-world style) analysis

`fixated` ships no visual world recording, so the same real data demonstrates the time-course workflow:
for every 100 ms bin after display onset, which area of interest (here: word) is fixated, and the proportion of
trials looking at each word. In a visual world study the AOIs would be target, competitor and distractors.

```{r}
onsets <- py$trials |> as_tibble() |> transmute(trial = as.integer(trial), display_on = as.numeric(display_on))
bins <- crossing(trial = onsets$trial, bin = seq(0, 1800, by = 100)) |>
  left_join(onsets, by = "trial") |>
  mutate(t = display_on + bin)

looks <- bins |>
  inner_join(fix, by = "trial", relationship = "many-to-many") |>
  filter(t >= start_time, t <= end_time) |>
  inner_join(roi, by = "trial", relationship = "many-to-many") |>
  filter(avg_x >= x_start, avg_x < x_end) |>
  count(bin, word_id)

props <- looks |> mutate(prop = n / n_distinct(bins$trial))
ggplot(props, aes(bin, prop, colour = factor(word_id))) +
  geom_line() + geom_point() +
  labs(x = "Time since display onset (ms)", y = "Proportion of trials fixating", colour = "Word")
```
